calc-ab-1-3-001.description: Graph of f. The left and right branches meet at a hollow point (2,5). A separate filled point is at (2,−1).

calc-ab-1-3-002.description: Graph of f. At x=−1 the left branch ends at hollow (−1,3), the right branch begins at hollow (−1,−2), and a filled point is at (−1,8).

calc-ab-1-3-003.description: Graph of f. The left branch approaches hollow (4,1); the right branch approaches hollow (4,−3). The filled point at x=4 has height 4.

calc-ab-1-3-004.description: Graph of f with a rising curved branch. Its two sides approach the hollow point (3,9). A separate filled point is at (3,2). Intermediate plotted vertices specify the displayed curve.

calc-ab-1-3-005.description: Graph of f. Left branch approaches hollow (0,7). Right branch approaches hollow (0,2). The actual value at x=0 is the filled point (0,6).

calc-ab-1-3-006.description: Graph of f consists of connected line segments through (−3,2), (1,−6), and (4,0). The vertex (1,−6) is included.

calc-ab-1-3-007.description: Graph of f near the domain endpoint −2. A left branch ends at hollow (−2,4). A separate filled point is at (−2,1). No right branch is shown or assumed.

calc-ab-1-3-008.description: Graph of f is a V made of line segments through (−4,5), (−1,2), and (2,5); its vertex is included.

calc-ab-1-3-009.description: Graph of f begins at the included endpoint (2,−3) and has only a right branch nearby. There are no domain values to the left of 2 near 2.

calc-ab-1-3-010.description: Graph of f. Two sloping branches meet at hollow (3,4), with a separate filled point at (3,9).

calc-ab-1-3-011.description: Graph of f. Horizontal branches have height 1 for −1<x<0, 2 for 0<x<1 and 1<x<2, 3 for 2<x<3, and −1 for 3<x<4. Branch endpoints are hollow, and f(1)=5 is a filled dot.

calc-ab-1-9-001.description: Two straight segments lie on y=x+2: the left reaches an open point at (3,5), and the right starts at that same open point. A separate filled point is at (3,0). No other branch occurs near x=3.

calc-ab-1-9-004.description: For x<1 a rising line y=x+1 ends with an open point at (1,2). For x>1 a rising line y=x−2 begins with an open point at (1,−1). A filled point at (1,4) gives the assigned value. These are the only branches near 1.

calc-ab-1-9-008.description: The left line rises to an open point at (−2,3). The right branch starts at that same open point, falls through (0,1), then rises through (2,3). A filled point at (−2,−1) is separate from both branches.

calc-ab-1-10-004.description: A straight line y=x+3 approaches the open point (0,3) from both sides. The only assigned value at x=0 is a separate filled point (0,5). There are no other branches near 0.

calc-ab-1-13-010.description: A descending line y=1−x approaches an open point at (3,−2) from both sides. A separate filled point at (3,4) is the currently assigned value. The branches near x=3 are otherwise unchanged.

calc-ab-2-3-004.description: The graph is piecewise linear. Its plotted vertices in order are (−3,4), (−1,3), (1,−1) and (3,0). In a whole neighborhood of x=0 it is the straight segment from (−1,3) to (1,−1).

calc-ab-2-3-005.description: A piecewise linear graph joins (−2,0), (0,2), (2,2) and (4,5). The entire segment from x=0 to x=2 is horizontal at height 2, with x=1 strictly inside that segment.

calc-ab-2-3-009.description: The piecewise linear graph passes through (−2,−1), (0,3), (2,7) and (3,8). Near x=1 it is the straight line segment joining (0,3) and (2,7), with both coordinates and numerical axis scales shown.

calc-ab-2-4-007.description: A continuous piecewise linear graph joins (−2,−3) to (0,1) and then to (2,−1). The two segments share their included point (0,1). Their slopes are respectively 2 on the left and −1 on the right, forming a corner at 0.

calc-ab-4-1-011.description: The horizontal axis is time t in minutes and the vertical axis is total scanned pages N(t). Straight segments join (0,0), (2,10), (4,22) and (6,26). Time 3 is inside the segment from (2,10) to (4,22).

calc-ab-4-2-007.description: The horizontal axis is time t in seconds, and the vertical axis is velocity v in meters per second. Straight segments join (0,−2), (2,2), (4,2) and (6,−2). Time 1 is strictly inside the first segment.

calc-ab-5-2-008.description: A continuous piecewise linear function on [0,5] joins closed point (0,−2), interior vertex (1,3), interior vertex (3,−1) and closed point (5,4) by straight segments. The point at x=1 is a peak near that input but is lower than the value at x=5.

calc-ab-5-3-005.description: This is the graph of f′, not f. Straight segments connect (−3,2), (−1,0), (1,−2), (3,0) and (5,2). Its values are negative exactly between x=−1 and x=3.

calc-ab-5-4-006.description: The graph is f′. Straight segments join (−2,2), (0,0), (1,−2), (2,0), (3,−2), (4,0), (5,2). It crosses from positive to negative at 0, touches zero from below at 2, and crosses from negative to positive at 4.

calc-ab-5-6-006.description: The graph is f′. Straight segments join (−2,−3), (1,−1) and (4,−4). All values are negative. The derivative graph increases from −2 to 1 and decreases from 1 to 4.

calc-ab-5-8-001.description: This graph is f. Straight segments join (−2,−1), (0,3), (2,3) and (4,−1). It is horizontal at height 3 on the entire segment from x=0 to x=2.

calc-ab-5-8-002.description: This graph is f′. Straight segments join (−2,−1), (0,1), (2,−1) and (4,1). Axis crossings occur at −1, 1 and 3; at 1 the sign crosses positive to negative.

calc-ab-5-8-005.description: This graph is f, a V made of straight segments from (−2,2) to (0,0) to (2,2). The left segment has slope −1 and the right segment slope +1. Both meet continuously at the corner.

calc-ab-5-8-008.description: This graph is f′, positive throughout the displayed interval. It rises linearly from (−2,1) to (0,3), then falls linearly to (2,1). Its peak at 0 has height 3, not zero.

calc-ab-5-8-011.description: This graph is f′, a horizontal segment at height −2 from x=−2 to x=3. In particular, f′ is the constant −2 throughout [0,2].

calc-ab-5-9-003.description: This is the graph of f″, the straight line from (−2,−2) to (2,2), crossing zero at 0. The separate given value is f′(0)=−2; it is not the height of this second-derivative graph.

calc-ab-5-9-004.description: This is f′, with straight segments through (−1,3),(0,0),(1,−1),(2,0),(3,3). It is zero at 0 and 2, decreasing until its minimum at 1, then increasing.

calc-ab-6-1-001.description: The graphed f is velocity v in m/s versus time t in seconds. Straight segments join (0,0), (2,4), (4,0) and (6,−2). The region from 0 to 4 is a triangle above the time axis; from 4 to 6 is a triangle below it.

calc-ab-6-1-006.description: The graphed f is velocity v in m/s versus time t in seconds. One straight segment joins (0,3) to (6,−3), crossing the time axis at t=3. The two triangular regions have equal areas on opposite sides of that axis.

calc-ab-6-1-008.description: The graphed f is a net queue growth rate in people per hour versus time t in hours. Straight segments join (0,1), (2,3) and (4,1). All rates are positive.

calc-ab-6-2-010.description: This graph is f, made of straight segments joining (0,2), (2,4) and (4,2). The midpoints of [0,2] and [2,4] have heights f(1)=3 and f(3)=3.

calc-ab-6-5-001.description: The graph is f, not its accumulation g. Straight segments join (0,−2), (2,2), (4,2) and (6,−2). The zeros of f are 1 and 5. The graph is positive between those zeros.

calc-ab-6-5-002.description: The graph is f. A straight line joins (0,2), (2,0) and (4,−2). Its triangular region from 0 to 2 is above the horizontal axis and has base 2 and height 2.

calc-ab-6-5-003.description: This graph is f. Straight segments join (0,−3), (2,−1) and (4,−2). On 0<x<2, f is negative and has slope +1.

calc-ab-6-5-007.description: This graph is f. Straight segments join (0,2), (2,−2), (4,−2) and (6,2). It crosses the axis at 1 and 5, and is negative between them.

calc-ab-6-5-008.description: This graph is f. A V of straight segments joins (−2,3), (0,1) and (2,3). Its slopes are −1 to the left of 0 and +1 to the right. The function stays positive, including f(0)=1.

calc-ab-6-5-009.description: The graph is f on [2,6]. Straight segments join (2,0), (3,3), (4,0) and (6,−6). The region on [2,4] is a triangle above the axis, and [4,6] gives a triangle below it.

calc-ab-7-3-001.description: Slope field on the integer grid −2≤x≤2, −2≤y≤2. Segments are horizontal along y=−x. At (1,1) the slope is 2; at (−1,−1) it is −2. Segment lengths are equal on the screen.

calc-ab-7-3-006.description: Slope field on the integer grid −2≤x≤2, −2≤y≤2. Slopes are zero on both axes, positive in quadrants I and III, and negative in quadrants II and IV. At (2,1) the slope is 2.

calc-ab-7-3-011.description: Slope field on the integer grid −2≤x≤2, −2≤y≤2. Rows y=−1 and y=1 have horizontal segments. Row y=0 has slope 1; rows y=−2 and y=2 have slope −3. Each row repeats across x.

calc-ab-7-4-001.description: Slope field for y′=y on the integer grid −2≤x≤2, −2≤y≤2. Positive rows slope upward, negative rows downward and the row y=0 is horizontal. A solution is required to pass through (0,1).

calc-ab-7-4-002.description: Slope field for y′=2x on the integer grid −2≤x≤2, −2≤y≤2. All slopes are negative left of the y-axis, zero on it and positive right of it. Each vertical column has a repeated slope.

calc-ab-7-4-003.description: Slope field for y′=x−y on the integer grid −2≤x≤2, −2≤y≤2. Segments are horizontal on y=x, upward below that line and downward above it. Consider the solution through (1,1).

calc-ab-7-4-008.description: Slope field for y′=−x/y at x=−2,−1,0,1,2 and y=−2,−1,1,2. The row y=0 is omitted because the equation is undefined there. In the upper-right quadrant slopes are negative. At x=0 and y≠0 the slope is zero.

calc-ab-8-1-003.description: The continuous graph of f consists of straight segments joining (0,−2), (2,2) and (4,0). It crosses the x-axis at x=1. Positive and negative triangular contributions must retain their signs.

calc-ab-8-2-005.description: This is the velocity graph, with straight segments joining (0,2), (1,0), (3,−2) and (4,0). Time is in seconds and velocity in meters per second. The initial position is 10 meters.

calc-ab-8-2-010.description: This is a velocity graph. Straight segments join (0,2), (2,−2) and (4,2). The velocity crosses zero at t=1 and t=3. Each of the four signed triangular pieces has area magnitude 1.

calc-ab-8-3-004.description: This is the net rate of change of the number of people in a hall, in people per minute. Straight segments join (0,4), (2,0), (4,−2) and (6,0). There are 100 people initially.

calc-ab-8-4-006.description: Two continuous boundaries on [0,4]. The upper boundary f consists of straight segments joining (0,3), (1,4) and (4,2). The lower boundary g is the horizontal segment from (0,1) to (4,1). Vertical boundaries at 0 and 4 close the region.
calc-ab-8-4-006.title: Boundary curves f and g
calc-ab-8-4-006.caption: Upper boundary f joins (0,3), (1,4), (4,2). Lower boundary g is y=1. Vertical endpoint lines close the region.

calc-ab-8-5-001.title: Region between x=y and x=4−y
calc-ab-8-5-001.description: The left boundary is the segment x=y from (0,0) to (2,2). The right boundary is x=4−y from (4,0) to (2,2). The horizontal segment y=0 closes the triangular region. Horizontal slice widths shrink from 4 at y=0 to 0 at y=2.
calc-ab-8-5-001.caption: Left: x=y. Right: x=4−y. Bottom: y=0. Integrate horizontal slice widths with respect to y.

calc-ab-8-6-001.title: Crossing boundaries f and g
calc-ab-8-6-001.description: The boundary f is piecewise linear through (−2,0), (−1,2), (0,0), (1,−3), (2,0). Boundary g is y=0 from x=−2 to x=2. Their intersections are −2,0,2. The left triangular region has area 2 and the right has area 3.
calc-ab-8-6-001.caption: f joins (−2,0), (−1,2), (0,0), (1,−3), (2,0). g is y=0. Find total area of both enclosed regions.

calc-ab-8-7-008.title: Base region under f
calc-ab-8-7-008.description: The base lies between y=0 and the piecewise-linear f joining (0,0), (1,2) and (3,0). Square sections perpendicular to the x-axis use the vertical segment in the base as their side. Thus f=2x on [0,1] and f=3−x on [1,3].
calc-ab-8-7-008.caption: Base: the region between the plotted f and y=0. Square cross sections have side length f(x).

calc-ab-8-8-007.title: Diameter function for semicircular sections
calc-ab-8-8-007.description: The base lies between y=0 and the piecewise-linear f through (0,0), (1,2), (3,0). At each x, f(x) is the diameter of a semicircular section perpendicular to x, not its radius.
calc-ab-8-8-007.caption: The plotted height f(x) is each semicircle’s diameter. Use area πf(x)²/8.
